_scope: ONE node: Map Candidate Fields. Only its position gate changes: the old `profileTextForPosition` + `matchesPosition(text)` pair is replaced by a title-based `matchesPosition(profileTitles(profile, experiences))`. Everything else in the node is byte-identical (the test cuts both gates out and compares the rest). No change to the location gate, the scorer, thresholds, queries, phase 2, the loop, completion or billing.
_theDefect: The gate searched one blob made of the headline, bio, industry and every job's title, company AND description, and passed a profile on ANY single word of the searched title as a SUBSTRING (after dropping level words and words of 2 letters, which also dropped 'hr'). When no word survived ('HR Assistant') it passed EVERYONE, including a profile with no title at all. Measured on the 14 retained real searches (1913-2048): the 8 people in another job who were delivered (7 under the live code) got through on 'business'/'partner' in a bio, headline or description (6), on 'generalist' in a headline (1), and on the pass-all with an empty profile (1). Each delivery is billed 6 credits when billing is enforced; the ledger itself was not read. 'HR' in a bio and a word in a company name are further paths the new gate also closes; neither caused a delivery in this data.
_ownerConstraint: The owner (2026-10-02): a candidate whose current title differs may have held the searched title in an earlier job, and must not be dropped. Measured: under the live code 36 of the 200 rows reaching the gate held the searched title ONLY in a past job and 27 of them were delivered (52 of 276 under each run's own, older location code, also 27 delivered). An exact current-title match would have lost all of them; a current-title-only version of this matcher would still have lost 23 of the 52 (9 delivered) plus 8 past same-field rows (1 delivered). Matching past titles was therefore made a requirement before any code was written.
_theRule: A profile passes when the searched role appears in one of its job TITLES: every experience title (current or past), each segment of the headline (split on '|' and bullets) and the occupation, both cut at ' at ' / '@' so a company named there never counts (a company written after '-' or ',' or in its own headline segment still does, as today). Titles and the searched title are normalised the same way: lowercase, diacritics removed, punctuation to spaces, and a short list of rewrites - 'human resources'/'h.r.' -> 'hr', 'hrbp', 'bd', 'purchasing' -> 'procurement', 'administrative'/'administration' and 'administrator' (except system/network/database/IT administrators) -> 'admin', 'salesman'/'salesperson'/... -> 'sales', 'telesales' -> 'tele sales', plural 'projects'/'operations'/'logistics'/'relations'/'systems', 'store keeper'/'store-keeper'/'stores keeper' -> 'storekeeper', QHSE/HSEQ/HSSE/EHS -> 'hse', 'health & safety' -> 'hse safety' and 'information technology' -> 'it technology' (the short form is ADDED, the words stay, so a 'Safety Officer' search still matches a past 'Health and Safety Officer'), 'i.t.' -> 'it', 'auditor'/'auditing' -> 'audit', 'mgr', 'asst', and 'M&E'/'C&B'/'R&D' joined as one word ('mne', 'cnb', 'rnd': never single letters, never the word 'me'). English words match WHOLE words; Arabic words match inside words, as before, so the article and feminine forms still match; an English search also accepts the Arabic title of the same job for a short list (sales, procurement, accountant/accounting, engineer, marketing). The searched title minus stop words, level words, one-letter tokens and two-letter Arabic words ('fi', 'min') gives its core; generic words (business, partner, generalist, development, admin, project, relation, ...) cannot carry a match alone: with at least one distinctive core word, any distinctive word in a title is enough; with none ('Business Development Specialist', 'Project Manager'), all core words must sit in ONE title; with no core at all ('Manager'), the title's own words must appear - the gate never passes everyone. HR searches also accept HR-family titles (hr, people, personnel, talent acquisition/management, recruitment, payroll, Arabic HR terms); the ROLE_PHRASES groups, the field-engineer and compensation & benefits families still apply, now to titles. An empty position still means no gate.

The replay script and its data stay outside this public repo.

byWhereTheRoleAppears.inNoTitleAtAll: 39 - 27 kept today, 0 kept. The 27 are per-search rows (about 19 distinct people; several recur across the 3 HR Business Partner and 2 HR Assistant searches), reviewed one by one by the author and independently by a reviewer: none is plausibly the searched role now or in a past job. E.g. university lecturers and 2 empty profiles for HR Assistant; CFOs, managing directors, a CEO/founder, a managing partner, a non-HR 'regional business partner', CTO/ERP founders and an Arabic sales/logistics profile for HR Business Partner; an operations manager and a marketing generalist for HR Generalist.

_measuredBeforeWriting.note: The categories are mechanical (role phrase / same field in current vs past titles); 'lost legitimate = 0' therefore rests on the per-row review of every dropped row, done twice independently, not on the categories alone. The 200 are per-search rows (at most 162 distinct title histories). The final code (after review round 1) gives exactly the same decisions on all 200 rows.

_expectedEffect: FEWER, cleaner candidates on HR searches above all (HR Business Partner, HR Assistant, HR Generalist), where the word-level and pass-all leaks concentrated; no measured change for Sales, Store, Account, Procurement and Business Development searches beyond profiles whose titles never named the role. Fewer AI evaluations wasted on other jobs. Delivery can fall slightly where the shortlist was padded by wrong-role people; phase 2 then tops up as it already does.
_knownLimits: Measured on 8 searched titles only. Whole-word matching is narrower than the old substring match even inside titles; the rewrites cover the spelling families found in review, but other morphology still differs: a role noun vs its field noun ('Accountant' vs 'Accounting Manager', 'Pharmacist' vs 'Pharmacy', 'Nurse' vs 'Nursing') matches neither today on titles nor now - today only when a description or bio named the role, which is the leak this removes.
GENERIC_TITLE_WORDS and the rewrites are judgement lists. A searched title made only of generic words needs all of them in one title.
No general plural or stem folding: 'Stores Manager' does not match 'Store Manager' (in Iraq usually a warehouse role), 'Accounts' does not match 'Account' (Account Manager vs accounting staff).

Arabic: Arabic searched words match inside Arabic title words, as today but only in titles. An English search accepts the Arabic title of the same job only for sales, procurement, accountant/accounting, engineer and marketing (HR via the HR family); for other English searches a profile whose role appears ONLY as an Arabic title is now dropped, where the old gate kept it if an English word of the title appeared anywhere in the profile. 0 such rows in the 200 measured. Full Arabic job-title support is a separate, later change (owner decision 2026-10-01).

Breadth that is deliberate but new: a search written in a variant form now reaches the whole family ('Salesman' finds every sales title, 'Purchasing Officer' every procurement title, 'Projects Manager' every project title, 'Administrative Assistant' every admin title). The English word 'it' in a headline ('Making it happen') matches an IT search (0 such headlines in the real data). Arabic level words (مدير, مساعد, موظف) still count as distinctive, as today, so an Arabic search such as 'مدير مبيعات' still keeps any Arabic manager title; ARABIC_FOR gives English searches the same breadth in Arabic as in English (e.g. 'Sales Engineer' accepts any مهندس or مبيعات title), and an Arabic company name written after 'في' still counts. These belong to the later Arabic change.

Profiles with no title anywhere (empty occupation, headline and experience titles) are now dropped for any searched title. 2 of the 200 measured rows were such profiles; one had been delivered with a score of 100 under an older scorer.

Generalization: no change on the 200 real rows, but synthetic and real-title probes showed false drops the old substring match avoided on titles alone - administrative/administration vs 'admin', Arabic article and feminine forms, plurals, salesman/salesperson, QHSE/HSE, 'Information Technology', 'Auditor', 'Mgr'/'Asst' in the search, 'Storekeeper' - and wrong-keeps from single letters ('M&E', 'R&D'); all fixed by the rewrites and Arabic handling above, each with a test. Runtime: confirmed on the production n8n container (n8n 2.25.6, Node v24.15.0, secure task-runner wrapper) that the Unicode regexes and the code run; no downstream node reads the old blob; Person Search profiles all pass (19/19 in the 2026-10-01 measurement). Claims: replay re-run independently and reproduced byte for byte; several statements in this record and the test header were corrected (leak paths, the 36/52 bases, 'never' for company names, 'billed'); two quasi-identifying synthetic examples were made neutral. Round 2 (one skeptic on the revised code): all round-1 fixes confirmed on 49 cases; it found and the code now fixes a crash on any search containing 'constructor' (prototype lookup in ARABIC_FOR, now Object.hasOwn), two rewrites that erased words and so dropped a PAST 'Health and Safety Officer' for 'Safety Officer' and 'Information Technology Manager' for 'Technology Manager' (now additive), non-IT 'Administrator' titles, two-letter Arabic search words, 'Store-Keeper' and 'Telesales' spellings, and the pronoun 'me' matching 'M&E'. Each has a test; the mutation battery (37 mutations, every rule removed or weakened one at a time) turns the test red every time, the identity run stays green, and the 200 real rows still give the same decisions.
